dict.string: Ask Claude and ChatGPT the same thing at once, in a new chat or in the chat each app already has open.
Opens a new chat in both and sends the question

# /usr/bin/python3 is a Command Line Tools shim that can prompt for an install. # Alfred spawns this from the GUI with a minimal PATH, where that prompt is # invisible and nothing happens at all, so prefer a real interpreter. # The query goes in as an argument, never through a shell. for py in /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 /usr/local/bin/python3 /usr/bin/python3; do [[ -x "${py}" ]] && exec "${py}" ai.py new "$1" done /usr/bin/osascript -e 'display notification "No python3 found" with title "Ask AI" subtitle "brew install python"'
Sends the text to the chat both apps already have open

# /usr/bin/python3 is a Command Line Tools shim that can prompt for an install. # Alfred spawns this from the GUI with a minimal PATH, where that prompt is # invisible and nothing happens at all, so prefer a real interpreter. # The query goes in as an argument, never through a shell. for py in /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 /usr/local/bin/python3 /usr/bin/python3; do [[ -x "${py}" ]] && exec "${py}" ai.py existing "$1" done /usr/bin/osascript -e 'display notification "No python3 found" with title "Ask AI" subtitle "brew install python"'

Keywords: nai, ai
`nai <question>` opens a new chat in both Claude and ChatGPT and sends the question. With no question it opens an empty new chat in each.
`ai <text>` sends the text to the chat each app already has open, rather than starting a new one.
An app that is not running is skipped and named in a notification. `nai` still opens its empty new chat there, but nothing is typed into an app that may still be showing a sign-in or update screen.
Neither app submits text handed to it on a URL, so both keywords press Escape, clear the composer, type the text and press Return. `nai` opens its empty new chat by URL first. Each app comes briefly to the front, because a keystroke goes to whatever is frontmost. The clipboard is left alone.
The Run Script objects set escaping to 0 rather than Alfred's 102, which the sibling workflows use. Both take the text as argv via scriptargtype 1 and never interpolate it into the script, so escaping cannot help here and would corrupt prose. Anything switching them to {query} must restore 102.
ai.py explains the rest.
